title: Lior and the Alibi
premise: Ines Vane, a true-crime podcaster haunted by the one case he never solved, is hired by a nervous stranger who pays triple to prove that a murder scheduled for the winter solstice will not happen. The target, Ines discovers, is the last living heir of the Harrow estate — and the murder weapon is a ledger disguised as a family Bible, its entries predicting deaths decades before they occur. As Ines races the solstice, he realizes the client is the future victim's own child, trying to prevent the very crime the ledger foretells. In the end, Ines must choose between exposing the ledger's author — the family's long-dead matriarch, whose 'prophecies' were really instructions — and letting the final entry come true, breaking the cycle by burning the record and giving the heir a life no one has written down.
about_author: Silas Amberdale is the pen name of a former court archivist who spent eleven years cataloguing wills, probate disputes, and unsolved estate crimes before turning to fiction. They write mysteries about paper trails, family secrets, and the quiet violence of inheritance.

chapters.title: The Client Who Paid for Nothing
chapters.summary: Ines Vane, mid-recording on a dead-end episode, receives an anonymous client offering triple his rate to prove a murder will not happen. The retainer arrives in cash with a single date: the winter solstice. POV: Ines. Beat: uneasy curiosity — a mystery that hasn't happened yet, and a man who has never turned down money.

chapters.title: Harrow House on the Hill
chapters.summary: Ines traces the retainer to Harrow House, a decaying estate whose last heir, Marguerite Harrow, hasn't left its walls in years. The staff are evasive; the groundskeeper recognizes Ines from his podcast and begs him to leave. POV: Ines. Beat: first dread — the house itself seems to know he's coming.

chapters.title: A Ledger Bound in Black
chapters.summary: Searching the estate's library, Ines finds a family Bible whose margins contain a ledger of dates and sums — each entry matching a Harrow death, recorded before it occurred. The final entry is blank but dated for the solstice. POV: Ines. Beat: cold shock — the case is real, and it's already half-written.

chapters.title: The Voice on the Answering Machine
chapters.summary: Ines interviews Marguerite, who is lucid, bitter, and insists the ledger is a joke her grandmother played. But a message on the estate's old answering machine, dated three days ago, whispers the solstice date in a voice Ines half-recognizes. POV: Ines. Beat: creeping paranoia — someone in the house is still writing.

chapters.title: What the Groundkeeper Buried
chapters.summary: The groundskeeper, Tomas, confesses that forty years ago he helped bury a Harrow cousin whose death never appeared in any record — proof the ledger can be beaten, or that it has a hidden volume. POV: Tomas. Beat: grief and guilt — a witness who stayed silent too long.

chapters.title: Episode Seven: The Harrow Tapes
chapters.summary: Ines airs a cautious episode on the Harrow ledger, and the client calls again: stop, or the solstice death becomes certain. The caller's voice is young — a child, or someone imitating one. POV: Ines. Beat: the stakes invert; his investigation may be the murder weapon.

chapters.title: Marguerite's Memory Palace
chapters.summary: Marguerite, softened by Ines's persistence, walks him through her childhood in the house, revealing that the ledger's 'prophecies' were read aloud to the children like bedtime stories. POV: Marguerite (via Ines's recording). Beat: tender horror — a childhood where death was homework.

chapters.title: The Second Ledger
chapters.summary: Following Tomas's burial site, Ines uncovers a tin box containing a second ledger — corrections, crossed-out dates, one entry for a death that was prevented. Someone once cheated the book. POV: Ines. Beat: hope, sharp and dangerous.

chapters.title: The Heir Apparent
chapters.summary: Ines discovers Marguerite had a child, given away in infancy — and that the client's voice matches a young woman, Rowan, who has been living in the village under another name. POV: Ines. Beat: the client and the target may be the same blood.

chapters.title: Rowan
chapters.summary: Ines confronts Rowan, who admits she hired him: the ledger's final entry is hers. Raised on the family's legend, she believes the book cannot be defied and wants proof it can — before she inherits the house and the habit of believing it. POV: Rowan. Beat: raw, defiant vulnerability.

chapters.title: The Solstice Approaches
chapters.summary: With nine days left, Ines cross-references both ledgers and finds the pattern: every 'prophecy' was self-fulfilled — the family read the book and made it true. The final entry is blank because it awaits a hand. POV: Ines. Beat: revelation — the murder hasn't happened because no one has decided yet.

chapters.title: Someone in the House
chapters.summary: The second ledger vanishes from Ines's hotel room, and Tomas is found unconscious at the estate gate. Someone inside Harrow House is protecting the book's authority. POV: Ines. Beat: fear closing in — the house has an immune system.

chapters.title: The Nurse Who Read Aloud
chapters.summary: Ines identifies the estate's longtime nurse, Edith, as the ledger's living custodian, trained by the matriarch to keep the family obedient to the book. Edith argues the ledger is mercy: it gives the family shape, certainty, an ending. POV: Edith. Beat: chilling conviction — the antagonist who believes she is kind.

chapters.title: Marguerite's Confession
chapters.summary: Marguerite admits she wrote the final blank entry's date herself, decades ago, to control Rowan's life the way her grandmother controlled hers — the murder is an inheritance of method, not a plan. POV: Marguerite. Beat: tragic self-awareness; the victim and the author are one.

chapters.title: Nine of Swords
chapters.summary: Rowan, convinced the ledger is fate after Edith shows her the 'accurate' entries, disappears toward Harrow House on the solstice eve. Ines's podcast feed is flooded with listeners predicting her death in the comments — the book is being read aloud again. POV: Rowan. Beat: despair — belief itself is the trap.

chapters.title: The Longest Night
chapters.summary: Solstice night. Ines breaks into Harrow House and finds Rowan in the library with the ledger open and a knife on the table — Edith's arrangement, a ritual meant to complete the entry. Marguerite watches from the stairs, unable to stop what she started. POV: Ines. Beat: the climax begins in silence.

chapters.title: The Blank Line
chapters.summary: Ines argues the only way to beat the book: the final entry requires a writer, not a victim. He offers Rowan the pen. Edith lunges; Marguerite, for the first time in forty years, moves to intervene. POV: Ines. Beat: the choice crystallized — authorship as the murder weapon.

chapters.title: Fire in the Library
chapters.summary: In the struggle, the Bible-ledger catches flame. Edith tries to save it and fails; Marguerite holds her back, whispering that the book never loved them. Rowan, pen in hand, writes nothing — and the solstice passes with everyone breathing. POV: Rowan. Beat: catharsis through refusal.

chapters.title: Ashes and Arithmetic
chapters.summary: In the aftermath, Ines reconstructs how the 'prophecies' worked: coercion, suggestion, and murder disguised as fate — including the buried cousin, killed by the first matriarch and recorded as prophecy. POV: Ines. Beat: sober clarity — the mystery solved, the horror accounted for.

chapters.title: What Ines Couldn't Solve
chapters.summary: Ines finally revisits the cold case that made him — and finds, in its files, a marginal note in the matriarch's hand. The Harrow ledger touched his life long before he knew it existed. POV: Ines. Beat: personal reckoning; the past was never past.

chapters.title: Episode Eight: Corrections
chapters.summary: Ines airs a final episode retracting the legend, naming Edith, and telling the truth about self-fulfilled prophecy. Listeners push back — they wanted the mystery to be magic. Rowan listens from the repaired house. POV: Ines. Beat: bitterswet vindication; truth is less loved than legend.

chapters.title: An Unwritten Year
chapters.summary: One year later, Marguerite and Rowan share the estate as family; Tomas tends a garden where the library burned. Ines receives no new client — only a blank notebook in the mail, with a note: 'Write something kind.' POV: Ines. Beat: resolution — a future with no entries yet, and that is the gift.
